This Privacy Policy explains what information the Wasdo Android application (the "App", "we", "us"), published by DappleByte, collects, how it is used and shared, and the choices you have. It applies to the App as distributed on Google Play. The App does not require you to create an account, and it shows no advertising.

Information We Collect

Product analytics

The App uses Google Analytics for Firebase to record low-frequency milestones such as onboarding steps, which screens are opened, whether a keyboard or mouse was detected, whether a mapping session started and how it ended, error conditions (for example, a failed input path together with your device brand, model and Android version), and the outcome of the purchase flow. For ready-made key layouts it also records which layout you imported and, when you move or delete one of its keys, that key's role (for example "fire"), a rough distance and direction, the game's version and a rough bucket for your screen shape, so we can find layouts that do not line up on some screens. If you use "Rate this layout", the App also sends the rating and options you pick and, only if you type one, a short comment of up to 100 characters, together with which layout it is, the game's version and the screen-shape bucket described above. Before the comment leaves your device, the App replaces anything that looks like an e-mail address, a web address or a phone number (7 or more digits in a row) with "[x]"; please do not include personal details in it. This tells us where users get stuck. Firebase assigns a random app instance identifier and derives your approximate country from your IP address; the IP address itself is not stored by us. Analytics data is kept for up to 14 months.

You can turn this off at any time under Settings → Send usage and crash reports. The App does not use the Android advertising ID: the permission that would read it is removed from the App, and advertising-ID collection is disabled in the analytics library.

Crash reports

The App uses Firebase Crashlytics to receive a report when the App crashes. A report contains the stack trace, the App version, your device model and Android version, the random installation identifier, and a short log of what the App was doing just before the crash (for example "mapping session started"). It never contains your key layouts, what you typed, or anything shown on your screen. The same Settings switch that controls analytics also controls crash reports.

Remote configuration

The App downloads a small set of configuration values from Firebase Remote Config (for example free-tier limits, feature switches and a list of games known to detect peripherals). Each request carries the random installation identifier, the App version, your device's language and country codes, time zone and Android version, as described in Google's Firebase documentation.

Ready-made layout updates

About once a day the App checks our website (dapplebyte.com) for a newer version of the ready-made layout library and, if there is one, downloads only the files that changed. Before use, the downloaded library is checked against our digital signature. These requests carry no identifier, no account and nothing about your own layouts. Like any web request, they reveal your IP address and a standard user-agent string (which includes your Android version and device model) to GitHub, which hosts our website and may keep them in its server logs; we do not receive those logs. This check can be switched off remotely.

Games you add to the App

When you add a game to your list inside the App, or when a key layout actually runs on that game, we record that game's package name (for example com.example.game) and the category reported by Google Play. We use this to decide which games receive ready-made key layouts first.

We record this only for games you add yourself, only for apps installed from Google Play, and at most once per game per device. We do not collect a list of the other apps installed on your device, and we do not record when or for how long you play. You can turn this off at any time under Settings → Help improve game support.

Purchases

The optional one-time Wasdo Pro purchase is processed by Google Play. We receive the purchase status needed to unlock Pro features and record whether the purchase succeeded, together with the product, price and currency, in our analytics. We never receive your payment card details.

Feedback email

If you choose to send feedback from the App, your email app opens with a pre-filled message containing technical details (App version, device model, Android version, language, whether the accessibility service is on, Pro status, which input path is in use, whether a keyboard or mouse is connected, the result of the last input self-check, and a list of the last 20 in-app events as event names and timings only, never key presses or game names). You can read the full text in the App before the email opens, and nothing is sent unless you send the email yourself. We use it only to answer you.

Share codes

If you choose to create a share code for a key layout, the App uploads that single layout (key positions, actions and the screen size it was made for) to our Firebase Cloud Storage through a Cloud Function and returns an 8-character code. The upload contains no device identifier, account or game progress. Anyone who has the code can download the layout for 90 days, after which it is deleted automatically. To limit abuse, each request carries a Firebase App Check token (which confirms the request comes from a genuine copy of the App via Google Play Integrity) and a random per-installation identifier used only to count how many codes an installation creates per day. Importing a code downloads that layout and nothing else; we do not record who imported it. The feature can be switched off remotely and nothing is uploaded unless you use it.

Google Play

Google Play provides us with aggregated install, rating and stability statistics for the App. The in-app rating prompt is shown by Google Play; the rating you leave goes to Google, not through the App.

What the App Does Not Collect

  • Key presses and mouse movement. While a layout is active, the App processes keyboard and mouse events on your device to perform the touches you configured. They are discarded as soon as they are handled and are never stored or uploaded.
  • Accessibility service. The App uses the Android Accessibility Service API only to perform the touches you configure. To do that it uses three things, all on your device: which app is in the foreground, to load the right layout and hide the floating pill elsewhere; your keyboard's keys while a layout is running; and your mouse's movement and buttons. It does not read, store or upload the text or content shown on your screen, what you type or your passwords. The App explains this before it opens the system Accessibility settings, and the service only starts if you turn it on there. The only thing the service may send is the package name of a game you added yourself, as described above, and you can turn that off.
  • Installed apps. The App does not request permission to see all apps installed on your device. The game picker can only see apps that have a launcher icon, and that list stays on your device and is never uploaded. The App also checks on your device whether our companion app Gamepad Pro is installed to show the right options. Only the games you add yourself are recorded, as described above.
  • Push notifications. The App does not send push notifications and does not register a push token.
  • We do not access your contacts, SMS, call logs, photos, microphone, camera or precise location, and the App does not read your phone number or advertising ID.

Permissions

These are the permissions the App declares, including those added by libraries it includes:

  • Internet and network state (INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE): sending analytics and crash reports, downloading remote configuration and ready-made layout updates, and Google Play Billing.
  • Ignore battery optimisation (REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS): an optional step that asks Android not to stop the accessibility service in the background while you play. You can decline it.
  • Google Play Billing (BILLING): the Pro purchase.
  • Companion app coordination (com.dapplebyte.wasdo.permission.SIBLING_ENTITLEMENT, com.dylan.gamepad.pro.permission.SIBLING_ENTITLEMENT): signature-level permissions that let only our own apps, signed with the same key, ask each other on your device whether one of them has a layout for the game you are playing, so the two apps never act on the same game at once. No other information is exchanged.
  • Vibration (VIBRATE): a short buzz replaces on-screen hints while stream mode hides the App's overlay.
  • Screen recording detection (DETECT_SCREEN_RECORDING, Android 15 and later): lets the App notice when screen recording starts so it can offer to hide its overlay. It does not record anything itself.
  • Library permissions (WAKE_LOCK, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE): added by Android's WorkManager scheduling library and by Firebase, which may read the Google Play install referrer to attribute installs. The App itself schedules no background work at boot and sends no notifications.

Data Stored on Your Device and in Your Backups

Your games list, key layouts and settings are stored on your device. Android's automatic backup may copy your games list, key layouts and Pro status to your own Google account so they come back when you reinstall or move to a new phone. That backup is controlled by your Google account settings, not by us, and we cannot read it. Analytics identifiers and the App's internal service health records are excluded from backup. You can export a layout to a file yourself; where that file goes is up to you.

How We Use Information

  • To provide the App's features, including Pro features you purchased;
  • To understand how the App is used, fix bugs and improve stability;
  • To decide which games to support first;
  • To prevent fraud and abuse and to comply with legal obligations.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not use it for advertising.

Sharing

  • Service providers that process data on our behalf: Google Firebase (Analytics, Crashlytics, Remote Config, and App Check, Cloud Functions and Cloud Storage for share codes), Google Play (billing and in-app review), and GitHub (hosting our website and the ready-made layout library).
  • Legal reasons: when required by law, or to protect our rights, users or the public.
  • Business transfers: if the App is sold or merged, information may be transferred as part of that transaction.

Third-party privacy policies

  • Google Analytics for Firebase and Crashlytics: firebase.google.com/support/privacy
  • Google Play: policies.google.com/privacy
  • GitHub: docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement

Your Choices

  • Turn off analytics and crash reports under Settings → Send usage and crash reports.
  • Turn off reporting of the games you add under Settings → Help improve game support.
  • Turn off the accessibility service at any time in your device's Accessibility settings; the App then cannot read input or perform touches.
  • Uninstalling the App stops all further collection and resets the installation identifier.

Retention

Analytics event data is kept for up to 14 months, after which it is deleted automatically. Crash reports are kept for 90 days. Aggregated statistics that cannot identify you may be kept longer.

Deleting Your Data

Because the App has no accounts, the data we hold is linked only to random identifiers. You can ask us to delete it by emailing us at the address below; we will respond within 30 days. Please note we may keep information we are legally required to keep.

Security

All data the App sends is encrypted in transit (HTTPS). No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, but we use commercially reasonable measures to protect it.

International Transfers

Our service providers may process information in countries other than yours, including the United States. Where required, they rely on appropriate safeguards for these transfers.

Children

The App is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, contact us and we will delete it.

Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time. Changes take effect when posted on this page, and the "Last updated" date above will change. Significant changes will also be announced in the App.

Contact Us

DappleByte
Email: feedback@dapplebyte.com

You can also use Settings → Feedback in the App.
